claims.text: A reducing pre-treatment yields a predominantly metallic PGM catalyst surface with minimal oxide formation.
A mild oxidizing pre-treatment will induce partial, sub-nanometric oxide formation on the PGM catalyst surface.
The resulting surface mediator consists of sub-nanometric oxide domains such as PtOx.
The oxide domains modulate the electronic properties of the PGM catalyst.
The oxide domains act as bifunctional catalytic sites.
The oxide domains facilitate oxygen transfer during ethanol oxidation.
The oxide domains facilitate proton transfer during ethanol oxidation.
Complete ethanol oxidation involves transfer of 12 electrons and 12 protons.
Electronic-structure modification by the oxide domains favors complete oxidation of ethanol.
The oxide domains help remove adsorbed intermediates or carbonaceous species that poison the catalyst.
The oxide domains may hinder nanoparticle sintering.
Suppressing carbonaceous poisoning and nanoparticle sintering improves catalyst durability.
Partial oxide coverage will increase ethanol-oxidation current density relative to a predominantly metallic surface.
Partial oxide coverage will increase selectivity toward complete oxidation products such as CO2 relative to partial products such as acetaldehyde.
Partial oxide coverage will slow performance degradation relative to a predominantly metallic surface.
The proposed beneficial mechanism applies at moderate operating potentials and after mild oxidizing pre-treatment.
Excessively oxidizing conditions may produce bulk oxide that blocks active sites and diminishes catalytic performance.
Highly reducing environments prevent formation of the beneficial sub-nanometric oxide domains.

contradictions.description: The boundary explicitly predicts that excessive oxidation and bulk oxide formation will deteriorate performance, whereas the falsification rule treats the same observation as falsifying the hypothesis. That observation supports the stated failure regime rather than falsifying the claimed benefit of partial oxidation.
